attempts.summary: On node1 (RHEL 7.9), installed lvm2 (via a temporary CentOS 7 vault repo since subscription-manager repos were disabled), built an LVM stack backed by two file-backed loop devices (no spare disk/partition existed — root partition was fully allocated), created VG vg_data and LV lv_data, formatted XFS, mounted at /srv/data, wrote test data, then grew the LV online from 900M to ~2.15GiB (filesystem to 2.2G) using vgextend+lvextend+xfs_growfs while the volume stayed mounted, with data integrity verified via sha256 checksums before and after. A systemd oneshot unit (lvm-loop-setup.service) was added to reattach the loop devices and activate the VG at boot, since loop devices don't persist automatically. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id/uptime/mount/checksum evidence, issued `shutdown -r now` in the background so the ack returned before disconnection, polled until SSH access returned, confirmed the boot_id and boot time changed (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce), and verified post-restart that the LV, VG, mount, and both test files (checksums) were all fully intact and healthy.
